note: One entry per source. 'display' says what the public site may show. Code licences are separate from data and media rights.

sources.name: NFL Big Data Bowl 2026 Analytics (2023 season tracking and coverage labels)
sources.licence_stated: CC BY-NC 4.0 on the data page (per the project handoff research; not re-read here)
sources.processing: local training and evaluation, under the rules the owner accepted
sources.display: public website display confirmed by the project owner on 2026-10-04: compact per-play exports for a sample of test plays; raw files are never published

sources.name: nflverse schedules/results (nfldata games.csv) and play-by-play
sources.licence_stated: CC BY 4.0 on the nflverse-data repository; the nfldata schedule file has no separate licence statement
sources.display: derived per-game features, probabilities and final scores

sources.name: SVHighlights, American-football subset (features, labels, loudness, transcripts, shots)
sources.attribution: Lee, Ki, Kang and Kim, SVHighlights, KDD 2026
sources.display: derived scores, loudness curves, labels, timestamps, links to the public source videos, and short transcript excerpts (100 characters or fewer). No video, no audio, no full transcripts. The dataset licence does not grant rights to the broadcasts themselves.

sources.name: NFL Health & Safety - Helmet Assignment (labelled helmet boxes, sideline and end-zone video, tracking for 60 plays)
sources.processing: local measurement of field calibration only; tables and one sample play extracted
sources.display: aggregate calibration error figures only. No video, frame, helmet box or tracking row is published

sources.name: Game video supplied by the project owner (high-school game, 2015)
sources.licence_stated: owner states it may be processed locally
sources.processing: local only, in data/local_media/ (ignored by Git)
sources.display: nothing: no frame, audio, cut or screenshot of it is published; only timings, durations and file hashes are reported

not_used.reason: removed from Kaggle at the host's request
another model's coverage predictions; never used as input or target
